script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for January 22. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

Light is electromagnetic radiation. What we call red is wavelengths around 700 nanometers; violet is around 400. Your eyes have three types of cone cells—sensitive to short, medium, and long wavelengths. Your brain combines their signals into the rich experience of color. Humans have 3 color receptors.  Mantis shrimp have 16.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Color reminds us that we don't see the world—we see our brain's interpretation of it.  Reality is always filtered through the lens of the perceiver.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Color Awareness - Really Seeing.

Here's your activity: Look around your current environment and count how many distinct colors you can identify. Push past the obvious—notice subtle variations and shades. Try to find at least 20 different colors. Appreciate that all of them exist only in your mind. This helps you heighten awareness of color in your environment.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about why we see colors can be applied to color awareness - really seeing. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
